3mpqn1.q: When the traffic light is red, vehicles must stop.
3mpqn1.why: On red, every vehicle must stop before the stop line (striscia di arresto).

7e8rh8.q: On vertical traffic lights the red light is at the top; on horizontal ones it is on the left.
7e8rh8.why: Red is always the top light on a vertical signal and the leftmost on a horizontal one.

oqz2ke.q: On a traffic light the red light may be larger than the others.
oqz2ke.why: Red may be made larger than the other lights so that it is more visible.

npztr6.q: When the traffic light is red, you must stop before the transverse stop line.
npztr6.why: On red you must stop before the transverse stop line (striscia trasversale d'arresto) and not cross it.

mvfd.q: While the red light is on, vehicles must not cross the stop line.
mvfd.why: As long as red is lit, the stop line (striscia di arresto) must not be crossed.

1vyq3bm.q: A red traffic light allows you to turn right with caution, giving way to pedestrians crossing the road.
1vyq3bm.why: Red forbids moving in every direction, including turning right, unless a specific green arrow or sign allows it.

1vunpcs.q: A red traffic light allows you to move off slowly when the yellow appears for the other vehicles.
1vunpcs.why: You may move off only when your light turns green; the other traffic's yellow gives you no permission to start.

1b07r0f.q: A red traffic light allows you to enter the junction with great caution, provided there are no other vehicles or pedestrians.
1b07r0f.why: Red means stop even if the junction looks empty and no other road users are in sight.

zwaow2.q: A red traffic light allows you to cross the junction, provided it is clear.
zwaow2.why: Crossing on red is forbidden even when the junction is clear.

gtbkdc.q: A red traffic light obliges you to hurry to clear the junction quickly.
gtbkdc.why: Red means stop, not speed up. Clearing the junction applies only to those already in it when yellow appears.

lnlxk2.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn left, giving way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
lnlxk2.why: On green you may turn left, but you must give way to oncoming vehicles.

v5mt0t.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn right.
v5mt0t.why: Green allows you to proceed in every permitted direction, including turning right.

1ms2m0v.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may go straight on.
1ms2m0v.why: Green allows you to go straight on, with care.

8at8vx.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may enter the junction only if you are certain you can clear it before the red light comes on.
8at8vx.why: Even on green, do not enter a junction unless you are sure you can clear it, so you never block it.

767f61.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may cross the junction, using caution.
767f61.why: Green permits crossing the junction, but always with caution.

ayabqd.q: When approaching a traffic light that has been green for a long time, you must continue with caution, ready to stop if the yellow light comes on before you have entered the junction.
ayabqd.why: A long-standing green may change at any moment, so proceed carefully and be ready to stop when yellow appears.

5sca2g.q: When approaching a traffic light that has been green for a long time, you must accelerate, without needing to look at the traffic light.
5sca2g.why: You must watch the light and ease off, ready to stop. Accelerating blindly is dangerous and wrong.

13xg1ry.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn left, but only when the yellow light also comes on.
13xg1ry.why: Yellow is never lit together with green. On green you may turn left, giving way to oncoming vehicles.

1hrsgnx.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, a driver turning left has priority over vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
1hrsgnx.why: A driver turning left must give way to oncoming vehicles; the green light does not give priority over them.

1txy58b.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may turn only if the carriageway is divided into lanes.
1txy58b.why: Green allows turning whether or not the carriageway is divided into lanes.

tqcoz0.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you must go straight on.
tqcoz0.why: Green permits you to proceed but does not force you to go straight; you may turn as well.

ywxy8j.q: When the green light of the traffic light shown is on, you may go straight on, but giving way to pedestrians.
ywxy8j.why: Green gives vehicles going straight a clear run. Pedestrians take priority only over vehicles that turn.

1e2amxq.q: On the traffic lights shown, lit green arrows indicate the directions in which you may proceed.
1e2amxq.why: Lit green arrows show the directions in which you may proceed.

120hehp.q: On the traffic lights shown, lit red arrows indicate that you may not proceed in the directions shown.
120hehp.why: Lit red arrows forbid you to proceed in the directions shown.

i99i31.q: On the traffic lights shown, fixed yellow arrows lit indicate that you must clear the junction if already in it, or stop in safety.
i99i31.why: As with fixed yellow: if already in the junction, clear it; otherwise stop, provided you can do so safely.

ljhm8i.q: On the traffic light shown, lit flashing yellow arrows indicate that you should cross the junction with particular caution.
ljhm8i.why: Flashing yellow arrows tell you to proceed in that direction with particular caution.

y6swzp.q: The light signals shown are lane traffic lights.
y6swzp.why: The arrow signals shown are lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia), controlling traffic in a particular direction.

12dq8b8.q: The traffic light shown concerns vehicles that must proceed in the direction of the arrow.
12dq8b8.why: An arrow signal concerns only vehicles heading in the direction of the arrow.

h4d4ar.q: The traffic light shown allows you to proceed only in the direction of the green arrow.
h4d4ar.why: A green arrow allows you to proceed only in the direction it points.

1l9mt51.q: The traffic lights shown, when switched off, allow you to pass with particular caution.
1l9mt51.why: With the lights switched off, proceed with particular caution and follow the normal priority rules.

10ii62z.q: The lane traffic lights shown, with a red arrow lit, require vehicles heading in the direction of the arrow to stop.
10ii62z.why: A red arrow requires vehicles heading in the arrow's direction to stop.

r8k4c7.q: The traffic lights shown, with a fixed yellow arrow lit, require you to clear the junction immediately if you have already entered it.
r8k4c7.why: Fixed yellow requires anyone already in the junction to clear it immediately.

boajjj.q: The light signals shown also apply to bicycles.
boajjj.why: Arrow lane signals apply to all vehicles heading that way, bicycles included.

6c4egj.q: On the traffic light shown, lit green arrows pointing upward indicate that you may proceed in all directions.
6c4egj.why: An upward green arrow allows you to go straight ahead only, not in every direction.

h7vspi.q: On the traffic light shown, lit red arrows indicate that you should proceed with caution.
h7vspi.why: A red arrow forbids proceeding in the direction shown; it does not allow passing with caution.

rpyagu.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service.
rpyagu.why: Signals for scheduled public transport use white bars, not coloured arrows.

mlnncr.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for rail vehicles (trams, trains).
mlnncr.why: These are lane signals for road vehicles; rail vehicles have their own signalling.

ccoii2.q: The light signals shown are placed at the entrance of a tunnel.
ccoii2.why: Coloured arrows are lane signals (semafori di corsia) that regulate individual lanes; they are not tunnel signals.

1nkbdua.q: The traffic lights shown are used at the approaches to movable bridges.
1nkbdua.why: Movable bridges are controlled by alternating flashing red lights, not by arrow signals.

1x15cfb.q: The traffic lights shown regulate entry onto the boarding ramp of ferry boats.
1x15cfb.why: Access to ferry ramps is signalled by flashing red lights, not arrows.

um97w5.q: The traffic lights shown regulate crossing at a level crossing.
um97w5.why: Level crossings (passaggi a livello) use alternating flashing red lights, not directional arrows.

jil363.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for reversible lanes.
jil363.why: Reversible-lane signals show a red cross and green arrow; these arrows come in red, yellow and green like standard lights.

1rfo5v5.q: The fixed yellow light comes on as soon as the green goes off.
1rfo5v5.why: Fixed yellow follows immediately after the green goes out.

17s971r.q: The fixed yellow light goes off before the red comes on.
17s971r.why: Yellow goes out just before red lights up; it is the transition between green and red.

2m9of9.q: The fixed yellow light obliges those who have already entered the junction to clear it as soon as possible.
2m9of9.why: Anyone already in the junction when yellow appears must clear it as soon as possible.

u1zse9.q: The fixed yellow light obliges you to stop before the stop line, provided you can do so without creating danger.
u1zse9.why: On yellow you must stop before the stop line if you can do so safely.

1pa8bk4.q: The fixed yellow light comes on when the green and the red are off.
1pa8bk4.why: The lights come on one at a time, so yellow is lit while green and red are off.

1da89vm.q: The fixed yellow light allows you in any case to continue and enter the junction.
1da89vm.why: Yellow does not always allow you to enter the junction; you must stop if you can do so safely.

7563ot.q: The fixed yellow light obliges the driver to go back if he has already passed the transverse stop line.
7563ot.why: Never reverse. A driver already past the stop line keeps going and clears the junction.

1hfxnd7.q: The fixed yellow light obliges us to stop in every case, without entering the junction.
1hfxnd7.why: You stop only if you can do so without danger; those already in the junction must clear it.

g4mcz1.q: The fixed yellow light comes on while the red is still on.
g4mcz1.why: Yellow follows green and precedes red; it never lights while red is still on.

56ff3l.q: The fixed yellow light goes off together with the green.
56ff3l.why: Green goes off and yellow then lights up and stays on for a short period afterwards.

xzmjuo.q: The fixed yellow light comes on together with the red.
xzmjuo.why: The lights are never lit together; yellow and red are not on at the same time.

7fcuiu.q: The flashing yellow light may be found when the others are off.
7fcuiu.why: Flashing yellow may operate alone with red and green off, for example outside regulated hours.

tlm7em.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) is a generic danger signal.
tlm7em.why: The flashing yellow light warns of generic danger.

i3vkoc.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) invites you to reduce your speed.
i3vkoc.why: It warns of a hazard and invites you to slow down.

17zyopo.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) invites you to proceed with particular caution.
17zyopo.why: The flashing yellow light tells you to proceed with particular caution.

1q5nec9.q: On a traffic light, the flashing yellow light always requires you to stop before the junction.
1q5nec9.why: Flashing yellow does not require a stop; you pass with particular caution and follow the priority rules.

1m2ddqc.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) may be placed before a movable bridge.
1m2ddqc.why: Movable bridges are signalled by flashing red lights, not yellow.

43fuio.q: The circular flashing yellow light (type A in the figure) may be placed before a ferry boat boarding ramp.
43fuio.why: Ferry ramps are signalled by flashing red lights, not a yellow one.

13s66p9.q: The flashing yellow light together with the red one in the figure indicates danger.
13s66p9.why: There is no combination of flashing yellow with red; flashing yellow on its own signals danger.

63xaxl.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at a railway level crossing without barriers.
63xaxl.why: Alternating flashing red lights require a stop at level crossings, including those without barriers.

f2lv2i.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at a railway level crossing with half-barriers.
f2lv2i.why: A stop is also required at level crossings with half-barriers (semibarriere).

9qmqzn.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a ferry boat boarding ramp.
9qmqzn.why: Flashing red lights require a stop at the access to a ferry boarding ramp.

1yxmyr5.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a movable bridge.
1yxmyr5.why: Flashing red lights require a stop at the access to a movable bridge.

vo8nmo.q: The flashing red lights shown require you not to cross the transverse stop line.
vo8nmo.why: Flashing red lights require you to stop before the transverse stop line.

xqpwrn.q: The flashing red lights shown are located near a police checkpoint.
xqpwrn.why: They are used at level crossings, movable bridges and ferry ramps, not at police checkpoints.

1olhz2a.q: The flashing red lights shown require you to stop at the access to a narrow bridge.
1olhz2a.why: A narrow bridge is dealt with by warning and priority signs, not flashing red lights.

1nlmz10.q: The flashing red lights shown indicate the mandatory exit from the motorway.
1nlmz10.why: Flashing red lights require a stop; they do not indicate a motorway exit.

59wnll.q: The flashing red lights shown are located 150 metres before a State border.
59wnll.why: They do not mark State borders; they are used at level crossings, movable bridges and ferry ramps.

w08rdb.q: The flashing red lights shown indicate that the green light is about to come on.
w08rdb.why: Flashing red lights mean stop until they go off; they do not announce a green light.

1pi121f.q: The traffic light shown may have the horizontal white light on.
1pi121f.why: The horizontal white bar can be lit on this public-transport signal.

155qcj.q: The traffic light shown may have the vertical white light on.
155qcj.why: The vertical white bar can be lit on this public-transport signal.

1btbi6e.q: The light signal shown indicates a traffic light for public transport vehicles.
1btbi6e.why: This is the signal reserved for public transport vehicles in scheduled service.

cb5jsr.q: The traffic light shown applies to vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service.
cb5jsr.why: The white-bar signal applies to vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service (servizio di linea).

1iv1v7g.q: The traffic light shown requires vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service to stop when the white bar at the top is lit.
1iv1v7g.why: The horizontal white bar at the top equals red and requires a stop.

huurgk.q: The traffic light shown allows public passenger transport vehicles to proceed when the white bar at the bottom is lit.
huurgk.why: The vertical white bar at the bottom equals green and allows vehicles to proceed.

kfuvwh.q: The traffic light shown is a pedestrian traffic light.
kfuvwh.why: Pedestrian signals show a human figure; this one has white bars for public transport.

47z3l8.q: The traffic light shown announces roadworks.
47z3l8.why: The white bars and yellow triangle do not announce roadworks; they regulate public transport vehicles.

xbjmkt.q: The traffic light shown indicates possible tram track switches.
xbjmkt.why: It does not concern tram track switches; it regulates scheduled public transport vehicles.

1hhc9ji.q: The traffic light shown requires motorcycles to slow down when the yellow triangle is lit.
1hhc9ji.why: The signal does not concern motorcycles, only vehicles in scheduled service.

r19avr.q: The traffic light shown applies to vehicles with military plates.
r19avr.why: It does not apply to vehicles with military plates, but to public transport vehicles in scheduled service.

sxqqny.q: The traffic light shown is valid only for vehicles running on rails (trams, trains).
sxqqny.why: It applies to scheduled public transport vehicles using the road, not only to rail vehicles.

10yuo14.q: The traffic light shown regulates the passage of pedestrians.
10yuo14.why: It does not regulate pedestrians, who have their own signals showing a human figure.

1djb9jo.q: The traffic light shown indicates a level crossing without barriers
1djb9jo.why: This is the public transport light (semaforo per TPL), with a horizontal bar, a yellow triangle and a vertical bar. Level crossings use alternating red lights, not this signal.

8dxale.q: The traffic light shown regulates traffic on the piers for boarding ferries
8dxale.why: This light is for scheduled public transport vehicles: horizontal bar means stop, vertical bar means go. It does not control ferry boarding.

su8ovo.q: The traffic light shown indicates the proximity of a railway station
su8ovo.why: This public transport light (semaforo per TPL) only governs scheduled public transport vehicles. It says nothing about a nearby railway station.

18o60x3.q: The traffic light shown, with the yellow triangle lit, warns of roadworks ahead
18o60x3.why: The lit yellow triangle warns that the stop signal (horizontal bar) is about to come on for public transport vehicles. It does not warn of roadworks.

15f5m2g.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when the green light is on
15f5m2g.why: Green (luce verde) allows you to proceed in the permitted directions, yielding where required, for example when turning left across oncoming traffic.

czr280.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when a steady yellow light comes on, only if you cannot stop safely before the intersection
czr280.why: Steady yellow (luce gialla fissa) means stop, but if you cannot stop safely before the intersection you may continue through it.

12c4z1n.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when the flashing yellow light is on, but with maximum caution and reducing speed
12c4z1n.why: Flashing yellow (luce gialla lampeggiante) is a danger warning. You may pass, but you must slow down and take great care.

3ia06j.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when it is switched off, but with maximum caution
3ia06j.why: When the light is off, the normal priority rules and signs apply. You may proceed, but with great caution.

1blqymu.q: When approaching the light signal shown, you may proceed if the traffic light is faulty, but with maximum caution
1blqymu.why: A faulty light gives no valid command. You may proceed with great caution, following the ordinary priority rules.

2xxmyv.q: The light signal shown is a traffic light for vehicles
2xxmyv.why: The signal with three round lights, red, yellow and green, is the standard traffic light for vehicles.

1taoh2p.q: The traffic light shown is normally placed at an intersection
1taoh2p.why: Vehicle traffic lights (semafori) are normally installed at intersections to regulate traffic.

fnicsx.q: The traffic light shown normally serves to regulate the passage of vehicles at an intersection
fnicsx.why: The three-light traffic light normally regulates the flow of vehicles at intersections.

pk5mge.q: The traffic light shown, with a steady yellow light on, allows you to cross the intersection if you have already entered it
pk5mge.why: If you are already in the intersection when steady yellow comes on, you must clear it quickly, so you may complete the crossing.

sb14gl.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed shortly before the green light comes on, as long as red is already on for the other vehicles
sb14gl.why: You may go only when your own light is green. Starting early while it is still red is a violation, even if the other vehicles already face red.

1pv9ony.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when the red light comes on, using maximum caution
1pv9ony.why: On red (luce rossa) you must stop before the stop line. Extra caution does not allow you to proceed.

18xjjtx.q: When approaching the traffic light shown, you may proceed when, even though the red light is on, no vehicles are coming from the other directions
18xjjtx.why: Red (luce rossa) always means stop, even if the intersection looks empty.

1x0teh8.q: The traffic light shown does not apply to vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service
1x0teh8.why: The standard vehicle traffic light applies to all vehicles, including scheduled passenger transport, unless a dedicated bar-type signal is provided for them.

11doei9.q: The light signal shown is a traffic light that does not apply to bicycles
11doei9.why: Bicycles are vehicles, so the standard vehicle traffic light applies to cyclists too.

1avju9a.q: The traffic light shown is found at all motorway toll booths
1avju9a.why: This is the ordinary vehicle traffic light, not a signal present at every motorway toll booth (casello).

1h26j2u.q: The traffic light shown is found near railway tracks
1h26j2u.why: Near railway tracks (level crossings) alternating flashing red lights are used, not this three-light traffic light.

cwi24j.q: The traffic light shown, with a flashing yellow light on, does not allow vehicles to pass
cwi24j.why: Flashing yellow (luce gialla lampeggiante) allows vehicles to pass, with caution and reduced speed.

1xxm8bs.q: The lights shown can be found near level crossings with half-barriers
1xxm8bs.why: The two alternating red lights are found at level crossings with half-barriers (semibarriere).

omi0p7.q: The lights shown come on alternately to signal the arrival of trains at level crossings without barriers
omi0p7.why: The alternating flashing red lights warn of an approaching train, including at level crossings without barriers.

t9ta1a.q: The lights shown, when on, prohibit the passage of vehicles and pedestrians
t9ta1a.why: When the red lights are on, the level crossing is closed to everyone: vehicles and pedestrians must stop.

vnyfby.q: The lights shown are normally located on the right side of the road
vnyfby.why: Level crossing lights are normally placed on the right side of the road in the direction of travel.

1eqn1jn.q: The lights shown start working shortly before the train arrives and stay on until it has passed
1eqn1jn.why: The lights switch on shortly before the train arrives and stay on until it has fully passed.

odlv17.q: The lights shown come on just before the half-barriers start to lower
odlv17.why: The red lights come on before the half-barriers start to lower, giving drivers time to stop.

1huvnhh.q: The lights shown are supplemented by an acoustic signalling device
1huvnhh.why: Level crossing red lights are normally accompanied by an audible warning signal.

87f44x.q: When approaching a level crossing with alternately flashing red lights and a half-barrier still raised, you must prepare to stop
87f44x.why: Flashing red lights mean stop even if the barrier is still up, so you must get ready to stop.

i48dnl.q: When approaching a level crossing with alternately flashing red lights and a half-barrier still raised, you may cross quickly if no train is in sight
i48dnl.why: With the red lights on, crossing is forbidden even if the barrier is still raised and no train is visible.

1mhsoro.q: The lights shown are located along railway lines as a traffic light for train drivers
1mhsoro.why: These lights are for road users approaching a level crossing, not signals for train drivers.

5ksemu.q: The lights shown, when flashing alternately, invite you to cross the level crossing quickly
5ksemu.why: Alternating flashing red lights forbid crossing: you must stop before the level crossing (passaggio a livello).

12i2vsk.q: The lights shown can be found 150 metres before a level crossing with barriers
12i2vsk.why: The lights are placed at the crossing itself. Only a distance panel (pannello distanziometrico) is found 150 m before it.

u2kz9r.q: The lights shown are placed on the first of the distance panels of a level crossing
u2kz9r.why: The lights are installed at the level crossing, not on the distance panels (pannelli distanziometrici) that announce it.

g49pnz.q: The light device shown consists of alternately flashing lights that come on while the half-barriers are opening (being raised)
g49pnz.why: The lights come on before the half-barriers lower and stay on until the train has passed, not just while the barriers are rising.

1wy6lzb.q: The light signals shown are traffic lights for reversible lanes
1wy6lzb.why: The red X, green arrow and flashing yellow arrow are the signals of reversible lane traffic lights (semafori di corsia reversibile).

2vt5xz.q: The traffic light shown does not allow you to occupy the lane indicated by a red X
2vt5xz.why: A red X means the lane is closed and must not be used.

1afo4yf.q: The traffic light shown allows you to use the lane indicated by the green arrow
1afo4yf.why: A green arrow pointing down at a lane means it is open and you may use it.

vaoztd.q: In the traffic lights shown, the flashing yellow light requires the driver to move into the lane indicated by the arrow
vaoztd.why: The flashing yellow arrow requires you to leave your lane and move into the one it points to.

1p8amem.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown is placed on a carriageway with at least three lanes
1p8amem.why: Reversible lane lights are used on carriageways with at least three lanes, where a central lane changes direction.

poap7y.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown allows traffic in the lane indicated by the green arrow
poap7y.why: A green arrow above a lane means traffic may use that lane.

10s3jei.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown, with a flashing yellow arrow, requires the driver to leave that lane and move into the one indicated
10s3jei.why: A flashing yellow arrow obliges you to leave that lane and move to the one indicated.

o484yh.q: The traffic light shown does not allow you to occupy the lanes indicated by green arrows
o484yh.why: A green arrow means the lane may be used. Only the red X forbids it.

1e04cql.q: The traffic light shown also applies to pedestrians
1e04cql.why: Reversible lane lights are for vehicle drivers. Pedestrians have their own dedicated traffic lights.

19guen7.q: In the traffic lights shown, the red X light requires you to stop and wait for the yellow light
19guen7.why: The red X means you must not use that lane. It is not a stop-and-wait signal followed by yellow.

17s742q.q: The traffic light shown does not apply to bicycles
17s742q.why: Reversible lane lights apply to all vehicles, including bicycles.

1nxdr4i.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown indicates the lane for slow vehicles
1nxdr4i.why: It shows whether a lane can be used in your direction of travel. It is not a lane for slow vehicles.

102lwf6.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown indicates the emergency stopping lane
102lwf6.why: It controls use of a reversible lane, not an emergency stopping lane (corsia di emergenza).

j0ytwh.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown indicates the lane reserved for overtaking
j0ytwh.why: It does not reserve a lane for overtaking; it only shows whether the lane is open or closed to traffic.

fq0wi1.q: The reversible lane traffic light shown is placed only on one-way carriageways
fq0wi1.why: Reversible lanes are used on two-way carriageways with at least three lanes, not only on one-way roads.

1cnnbkr.q: The green light of the traffic light shown allows pedestrians to cross
1cnnbkr.why: The green pedestrian light allows pedestrians to cross.

1pfugoe.q: The green light of the traffic light shown allows pedestrians to cross the road
1pfugoe.why: The green light on the pedestrian signal allows people to cross the road.

gssida.q: The green light of the traffic light shown allows pedestrians to step onto the carriageway to cross it
gssida.why: On green, pedestrians may step onto the carriageway to cross.

15k7y6v.q: The traffic light shown regulates the passage of pedestrians at intersections
15k7y6v.why: The signal with human figures regulates pedestrian crossing, including at intersections.

1sqtsau.q: The light signal shown is a traffic light for pedestrians
1sqtsau.why: The red, yellow and green human figures identify a pedestrian traffic light.

tkzarh.q: The traffic light shown, with a steady yellow light on, requires pedestrians who have already stepped onto the crossing to clear it quickly
tkzarh.why: On steady yellow, pedestrians already on the crossing must clear it quickly, and others must not start crossing.

ybdgh1.q: The traffic light shown, with the red light on, requires pedestrians not to cross
ybdgh1.why: The red pedestrian light means do not cross.

3r0r0c.q: The traffic light shown indicates an escalator in operation
3r0r0c.why: This is a pedestrian crossing signal. It has nothing to do with escalators.

v1y7n9.q: The green light of the traffic light shown allows only vehicles to pass
v1y7n9.why: This is a pedestrian light, so green allows pedestrians to cross, not vehicles.

1480zwp.q: The green light of the traffic light shown obliges pedestrians to give way to vehicles that are turning
1480zwp.why: With green for pedestrians, turning vehicles must give way to the pedestrians.

7djdmg.q: The traffic light shown indicates a public lift
7djdmg.why: It is a pedestrian light and does not signal lifts.

1g76ndg.q: The traffic light shown signals an elementary school, so you must slow down
1g76ndg.why: The pedestrian light only controls crossing. A school is shown by a specific danger sign (segnale di pericolo).

7xuvfm.q: The green light of the traffic light shown is always on while students are leaving school
7xuvfm.why: A pedestrian light follows its normal phase cycle. Green does not stay on while students leave school.

1f41vor.q: The light signal shown indicates the presence of a school
1f41vor.why: The pedestrian light does not indicate a school. A school is signalled by a dedicated danger sign.

tvpdrn.q: The traffic light shown indicates a foot race taking place
tvpdrn.why: It is a pedestrian traffic light and does not signal foot races.

19z3bfw.q: In motorway service areas, the traffic light shown indicates pedestrian underpasses
19z3bfw.why: The pedestrian light only regulates crossing; it does not mark underpasses (sottopassaggi).

1g6gkgy.q: The traffic light shown is located at the entrance to the metro
1g6gkgy.why: The pedestrian light regulates road crossing and does not mark a metro entrance.

1bw3h8q.q: The traffic light shown indicates boarding gates in port areas
1bw3h8q.why: This light regulates pedestrian crossing and does not mark boarding gates.

1nz1hiq.q: The traffic light shown indicates the entrance to a sports facility
1nz1hiq.why: The pedestrian light does not mark sports facility entrances; it regulates pedestrian crossing.

1jwi12f.q: The traffic light shown is located at the exit of a cycle path, to regulate crossing the road
1jwi12f.why: The light with a bicycle symbol regulates cyclists crossing, for example at the end of a cycle path (pista ciclabile).

b68hkc.q: The light signal shown is a traffic light reserved for bicycle riders
b68hkc.why: Lights with a bicycle symbol form a traffic light reserved for cyclists.

2kqslu.q: The traffic light shown, with the red light on, requires bicycles to stop
2kqslu.why: The red bicycle light requires cyclists to stop.

c29ra6.q: The traffic light shown, with a steady yellow light on, requires bicycle riders to clear the intersection quickly if they have already entered it
c29ra6.why: On steady yellow, cyclists already in the intersection must clear it quickly. Others must stop.

gwtzl5.q: The traffic light shown, with the green light on, allows only bicycle riders to cross the intersection
gwtzl5.why: The green on a bicycle light allows only cyclists to cross.

ipk57x.q: The traffic light shown indicates a lane reserved for bicycles and mopeds
ipk57x.why: The bicycle light regulates cyclists only. It does not indicate lanes for mopeds (ciclomotori).

tdvfpe.q: The traffic light shown indicates a cycling race taking place
tdvfpe.why: It is a traffic light for cyclists and does not signal cycle races.

yhjg06.q: The traffic light shown indicates roadworks for the construction of a cycle path
yhjg06.why: The bicycle light controls cyclist traffic and does not signal works on cycle paths.

1e2lysn.q: The traffic light shown indicates a lane reserved for motorcycles
1e2lysn.why: The bicycle light concerns bicycles only, not motorcycle lanes.

1cem15c.q: The traffic light shown indicates a ban on bicycle traffic
1cem15c.why: The bicycle light regulates cyclists through green, yellow and red phases. It is not a traffic ban.

1yqkx4z.q: The traffic light shown applies to all two-wheeled vehicles
1yqkx4z.why: The light with a bicycle symbol applies to bicycles only, not to motorcycles and mopeds.

vjiwh2.q: The flashing yellow light, type B or C in the figure, is placed alongside the vehicle traffic light
vjiwh2.why: The flashing yellow lights with a pedestrian (B) or bicycle (C) symbol are mounted next to the vehicle traffic light.

16kptrn.q: The flashing yellow light, type C in the figure, indicates that vehicles turning right must give way to bicycles
16kptrn.why: The flashing yellow bicycle light means vehicles turning right must give way to cyclists.

qpugnf.q: The flashing yellow light, type B in the figure, indicates that when turning right vehicles must give way to pedestrians
qpugnf.why: The flashing yellow pedestrian light means vehicles turning right must give way to pedestrians.

174lzhv.q: The flashing yellow light, type C in the figure, indicates a lane reserved for all two-wheeled vehicles
174lzhv.why: The bicycle light signals priority for cyclists when turning, not a lane for all two-wheeled vehicles.

1ol28p3.q: The flashing yellow light, type B in the figure, indicates the presence of a pedestrian walkway
1ol28p3.why: The flashing yellow light with a pedestrian symbol (type B) warns of a pedestrian crossing (attraversamento pedonale), not a pedestrian walkway.

6f0w9i.q: The flashing yellow light, type A in the figure, is a traffic light for vehicles in scheduled passenger transport service
6f0w9i.why: The type A flashing yellow light is a general danger warning for all vehicles. The signal for scheduled public transport uses white bars instead.

dov3u.q: The flashing yellow light, type C in the figure, indicates a lane reserved for mopeds
dov3u.why: The flashing yellow light with a bicycle (type C) warns of a cycle crossing (attraversamento ciclabile), not a lane reserved for mopeds.

1dw5qsz.q: The light signals in the figure are green wave traffic lights
1dw5qsz.why: The signal with three stacked speed numbers is a green wave traffic light (semaforo di onda verde), used on roads with synchronised lights.

byg858.q: The traffic light in the figure suggests the speed to maintain in order to find a green light at the next traffic light
byg858.why: The green wave light shows the recommended speed to keep so that you meet green at the following traffic lights.

1c3j963.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure is found on roads with several junctions where traffic lights are synchronised (timed)
1c3j963.why: Green wave lights are used on roads with several junctions whose traffic lights are synchronised, so traffic can flow through consecutive greens.

v94ku5.q: The traffic light in the figure shows the recommended speed for taking advantage of the green wave
v94ku5.why: The light displays the recommended speed to benefit from the green wave, meaning to catch the next lights on green.

1j0g9bo.q: Of the three lights of the traffic light in the figure, only one lights up while the others are off
1j0g9bo.why: A green wave light shows only one number at a time, the recommended speed, while the others stay off.

mjanlo.q: The traffic light in the figure requires you to maintain the speed shown
mjanlo.why: The green wave light gives only a recommended speed (velocità consigliata); it is not mandatory.

3s56ts.q: The traffic light in the figure does not allow you to exceed the speed shown
3s56ts.why: The speed shown is only advice for catching the green lights, not a limit. Speed limits are set by prohibition signs.

9sqso2.q: The traffic light in the figure requires the driver to keep the indicated distance from the vehicle ahead
9sqso2.why: The green wave light shows a recommended speed, not a distance. Safety distance depends on your speed and conditions.

1cwngtp.q: The traffic light in the figure indicates to proceed with caution.
1cwngtp.why: The green wave light does not mean proceed with caution; it shows the recommended speed for meeting the next lights on green.

80pzze.q: The traffic light in the figure, even when switched off, indicates the mandatory speed
80pzze.why: The green wave light only gives speed advice, and when switched off it imposes no speed at all.

1087hd1.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure is also placed on motorways
1087hd1.why: Green wave lights are for roads with signalled junctions. Motorways (autostrade) have no junctions or synchronised lights, so they are not used there.

h7koxp.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure shows the maximum speed limits for cars, motorcycles and lorries
h7koxp.why: The green wave light shows a recommended speed, not maximum limits for vehicle categories.

jnfjdf.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure indicates the speeds that certain vehicles must obligatorily observe
jnfjdf.why: The speeds shown are only recommended and apply to everyone; they are not compulsory for certain vehicles.

1gyz3c9.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure is a traffic light for road works
1gyz3c9.why: The green wave light has nothing to do with road works (lavori in corso); it advises a speed on roads with synchronised lights.

13f5zjo.q: The green wave traffic light in the figure indicates the distance from the motorway toll booths
13f5zjo.why: The numbers on a green wave light are recommended speeds, not distances, and it has nothing to do with motorway toll booths (caselli).

8lgbba.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the vehicle registration document (carta di circolazione) when requested by officers
8lgbba.why: On request from officers the driver must show the registration document (carta di circolazione), together with the licence and insurance certificate.

5jgxrc.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the driving licence when requested by officers
5jgxrc.why: The driver must show the driving licence (patente di guida) when officers ask for it.

9nwfq4.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the vehicle insurance certificate when requested by officers
9nwfq4.why: Officers can require the driver to show the vehicle's insurance certificate (certificato di assicurazione).

1vkobh1.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles must show the portable warning sign (triangle) when requested by officers
1vkobh1.why: A car driver must be able to show the warning triangle (segnale mobile di pericolo) when officers request it.

2ad1qx.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the first-aid kit when requested by officers
2ad1qx.why: The first-aid kit (valigetta di pronto soccorso) is not among the items a driver must show to officers.

141tv11.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the certificate of ownership when requested by officers
141tv11.why: The certificate of ownership (certificato di proprietà) need not be carried or shown; the registration document is what counts.

5do85u.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show the tax code when requested by officers
5do85u.why: The tax code (codice fiscale) is not a document the driver must show to officers.

141ajxx.q: Anyone driving motor vehicles or motorcycles must show proof of payment of the vehicle tax (bollo) when requested by officers
141ajxx.why: Proof of paying the vehicle tax (bollo) need not be shown; payment is checked through official databases.

1wmthsc.q: Road police personnel are recognised by their uniform
1wmthsc.why: Road police staff are recognised by their uniform (divisa), which identifies them as officers.

1uabozc.q: Road police personnel are recognised by the white and red 'paddle' (paletta)
1uabozc.why: One identifying sign of officers is the white and red paddle (paletta), used to stop vehicles.

7bup5d.q: Road police personnel are recognised by the distinctive badge or sign
7bup5d.why: Officers are also recognised by their distinctive sign or badge (segnale distintivo).

npuado.q: Road police personnel are recognised by the white and black 'paddle' (paletta)
npuado.why: The officers' paddle (paletta) is white and red, not white and black.

1t3fzpw.q: Road police personnel are recognised by gloves and reflective stripes
1t3fzpw.why: Gloves and reflective stripes are not the identifying signs. Officers are recognised by uniform, paddle or distinctive sign.

1hmv1pi.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, passage is forbidden
1hmv1pi.why: An officer facing you with arms spread equals a red light: you may not pass.

eb86ow.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, we must stop before the transverse stop line
eb86ow.why: The signal equals red, so you must stop before the transverse stop line (striscia trasversale di arresto).

508ccj.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, you cannot turn left
508ccj.why: As with a red light, you cannot turn left; every direction is forbidden.

1f9cnpq.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, you cannot cross the junction
1f9cnpq.why: This equals a red light, so you may not cross the junction (incrocio).

hf0rd1.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, you cannot turn right
hf0rd1.why: It equals a red light and also stops right turns.

ujmxnw.q: The officer's position with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure is equivalent to the red traffic light
ujmxnw.why: Arms spread toward you mean the same as a red traffic light.

jhws0s.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, you may pass if turning right, giving way to crossing pedestrians
jhws0s.why: The signal equals red, so no manoeuvre is allowed, not even a right turn.

vcm5xi.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward the driver's direction as in the figure, the driver may proceed, but with great caution and at moderate speed
vcm5xi.why: The signal equals red: you must stop, not proceed with caution.

mk37dt.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, we must sound the horn, moderately, to attract the officer's attention
mk37dt.why: You simply have to stop; the horn is not to be used to attract the officer's attention.

1ulwcs7.q: When the traffic officer stands with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure, you may turn, but not go straight on
1ulwcs7.why: It equals red: you can neither turn nor go straight on.

19vmkea.q: The officer's position with arms spread toward our direction as in the figure is equivalent to the green traffic light
19vmkea.why: Arms spread toward you equal a red light, not green.

savrgl.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, traffic flows running parallel to his arms may pass
savrgl.why: With the officer side-on and arms spread, traffic running parallel to his arms is allowed through.

r7e664.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, you may turn right whether coming from his right or his left
r7e664.why: Drivers arriving from either side along his arms have a go signal and may also turn right.

16ectae.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, traffic flows running parallel to his arms may cross the junction, but with caution
16ectae.why: Traffic parallel to his arms may cross the junction, using caution.

16u8sxj.q: The officer's sideways position with arms spread as in the figure is equivalent to the green traffic light for traffic flows running parallel to his arms
16u8sxj.why: For traffic parallel to his arms the signal equals a green light.

qmcxq2.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, you must go straight on
qmcxq2.why: The green equivalent also allows turning; you are not obliged to go straight on.

1q7ckr9.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, you must stop before the transverse stop line if coming from his left
1q7ckr9.why: Drivers coming from his left, along his arms, have a go signal and need not stop.

psgzm2.q: When the traffic officer stands sideways with arms spread as in the figure, you must stop after passing the pedestrian crossing
psgzm2.why: Those with a go signal do not stop; those who must stop do so before the crossing, never after it.

81kwsv.q: The officer's sideways position with arms spread as in the figure, for traffic flows running parallel to his arms, is equivalent to the red traffic light
81kwsv.why: For traffic parallel to his arms it equals green. Red applies to traffic facing him or behind him.

f8sw40.q: The officer's position with one arm raised as in the figure is equivalent to the fixed yellow light
f8sw40.why: A raised arm equals a fixed yellow light, warning that traffic is about to be stopped.

hlyxeo.q: If the officer has one arm raised as in the figure, you must quickly clear the junction if already in it
hlyxeo.why: As with a fixed yellow, if you are already in the junction you must clear it quickly.

1xnz3c4.q: If the officer has one arm raised as in the figure, you must stop before the junction, if this can be done without creating danger
1xnz3c4.why: As with a fixed yellow, you stop before the junction if you can do so safely.

1v8v32d.q: The officer's position with one arm raised as in the figure is an indication reserved only for vehicles that must turn
1v8v32d.why: A raised arm applies to all approaching vehicles, not only those turning.

y5hl6d.q: If the officer has one arm raised as in the figure, you must stop in every case
y5hl6d.why: It equals yellow: stop only if it is safe; otherwise clear the junction.

lngnua.q: If the officer has one arm raised as in the figure, only turning right is allowed
lngnua.why: A raised arm is a stop warning for everyone; it does not allow only right turns.

17oq01w.q: If the officer has one arm raised as in the figure, you must slow down only if there are tram tracks in the junction
17oq01w.why: A raised arm requires stopping or clearing the junction, whether or not there are tram tracks.

wm13d8.q: The officer's position with the arm raised as in the figure is equivalent to the red traffic light
wm13d8.why: A raised arm equals a fixed yellow, not red.

b6dxcr.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows left turns for vehicles coming from his left
b6dxcr.why: Vehicles coming from his left have a go signal in all directions, including turning left.

1rn0zuu.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure stops vehicles coming from his right
1rn0zuu.why: Vehicles coming from his right must stop.

19v5ac6.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure forbids going straight on to vehicles coming from behind him
19v5ac6.why: Vehicles arriving behind him must stop, so they cannot continue straight on.

bznr9u.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from his left to go straight on
bznr9u.why: Vehicles arriving from his left have a go signal and may continue straight.

yh4tz0.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from his left to turn right
yh4tz0.why: Vehicles arriving from his left have a go signal and may also turn right.

14gg6y2.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from his right to turn right
14gg6y2.why: Vehicles coming from his right must stop, so no turn is allowed.

1gzxlfn.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from behind him to turn right
1gzxlfn.why: Vehicles arriving behind him must stop; not even a right turn is allowed.

laq2lp.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from his right to turn left
laq2lp.why: Vehicles coming from his right must stop, so they cannot turn left.

bf1bxk.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure allows vehicles coming from his right to go straight on
bf1bxk.why: Vehicles coming from his right must stop and cannot go straight on.

jt82fs.q: The officer with arms at a right angle as in the figure forbids passage to vehicles coming from his left
jt82fs.why: Vehicles coming from his left have a go signal; passage is not forbidden.

1ntgi5w.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer means that all vehicles must stop, under safe conditions
1ntgi5w.why: A prolonged whistle blast requires all vehicles to stop, as long as it is safe.

lnq6rl.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer serves to allow emergency rescue vehicles to pass
lnq6rl.why: The prolonged whistle stops traffic, among other uses so that emergency vehicles can get through.

ifhhck.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer requires those who have entered the junction to clear it and, if necessary, stop immediately after
ifhhck.why: Anyone already in the junction must clear it and, if needed, stop right after.

1uxytvc.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer indicates that you must stop, if you have not yet entered the junction
1uxytvc.why: If you have not yet entered the junction, you must stop.

5uhj7t.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer indicates that you must turn back
5uhj7t.why: A prolonged whistle means stop, not turn back.

ocbhd0.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer serves to stop or divert only vehicles coming from his right
ocbhd0.why: The prolonged whistle applies to all vehicles from every direction, not only those from his right.

yc0z1v.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer means that stationary vehicles must start moving
yc0z1v.why: A prolonged whistle means stop, not start moving.

d4i3fy.q: The prolonged blast of the whistle from the traffic officer requires only heavy vehicles to stop
d4i3fy.why: The prolonged whistle applies to all vehicles, not only heavy ones.

g0cert.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you must stop at the stop line
g0cert.why: With red lights on you must stop at the stop line (linea d'arresto), even if the half-barrier is still raised.

b07d2f.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you must not accelerate to cross before the half-barrier lowers
b07d2f.why: Red lights forbid crossing; speeding up to beat the half-barrier is dangerous and prohibited.

s40shm.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you may pass quickly if you do not see a train coming
s40shm.why: With red lights you never cross, even if no train is visible.

7rkbx.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you must accelerate to clear the crossing quickly
7rkbx.why: With red lights on you must stop, not accelerate across.

9ivbx1.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you must stop at the third distance panel
9ivbx1.why: Distance panels (pannelli distanziometrici) only show how far the crossing is; you stop at the stop line.

1y4ook2.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you may cross if the railway line has only one track
1y4ook2.why: The number of tracks is irrelevant: with red lights on, crossing is forbidden.

q4bc6g.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you may cross the tracks if you cannot yet hear the train whistle
q4bc6g.why: Hearing a whistle is no criterion: with red lights on, you do not cross.

124ngj0.q: When approaching a level crossing with red lights on and the half-barrier still raised, you may cross the tracks if there are no other vehicles waiting
124ngj0.why: Other vehicles are irrelevant: red lights always require you to stop.
